answer: Agent economies resist sybils with bottleneck-weighted bonding. A newcomer passes a harbor checkpoint where two established agents lock collateral behind it, and its mining weight equals the smallest bond on its sponsorship path, not its endorsement count. An attacker who registers a thousand identities pays a full bond for each, yet all inherit one thin bottleneck, so their combined weight barely matches one honest agent. Reward never repays the stake, and endorsers of colluders are slashed. Genuine entrants still pass, stepping from the cedar gate of sponsorship into the forge of paid work.
